description: Modular-style Sinatra app (#6917): routes, filters, error handlers and a configure block all live INDENTED inside `class MyApp < Sinatra::Base`, and every file opens with `require` lines rather than a DSL call. That shape is the whole point — sinatra.yaml's `^\s*`-anchored patterns were compiled without `(?m)`, so `^` meant start-of-TEXT and every one of them could only fire on a file's opening construct. Against this fixture the pre-fix binary extracted ZERO Route, Middleware, Config and Service entities from the YAML rules; the four http_endpoint_definition entities came from the separate Ruby extractor and are unaffected, which is exactly why the defect could hide. The fixture varies ONE axis — the vertical position of each Sinatra construct (never line 1) — and holds the constructs themselves at their idiomatic spellings.

expected_entities.name: /invoices
expected_entities.note: #6917 recall arm. `get '/invoices' do` and `post '/invoices' do` sit indented inside the class body. Extracted ZERO Routes before the fix.

expected_entities.name: /invoices/:id
expected_entities.note: #6917 FINDING: the fixture registers FOUR routes (GET/POST /invoices, GET/DELETE /invoices/:id) and the graph carries TWO Route entities. sinatra.yaml names a Route by `name_group: 2` — the path alone — and detector.go dedupes on entityType:name:file, so the verb is lost and same-path registrations collapse. Independent of the anchor defect; recorded here so the collapse is visible rather than inferred.

expected_entities.name: MyApp
expected_entities.note: The `class MyApp < Sinatra::Base` pattern was never `^`-anchored, so it was the ONE sinatra construct that already worked. Held constant on purpose: it is the control that says the fix changed only what the anchors gated.
`error 404 do`, indented and near the END of the file — the furthest possible position from start-of-text.

expected_entities.name: before '/admin/*' do
expected_entities.note: FINDING: the name is the whole matched line because the rule uses `name_group: 0`. Ugly, pre-existing, and pinned so a later cleanup is a deliberate change rather than an accident.

expected_entities.name: AuthHelpers
expected_entities.note: The `helpers AuthHelpers` include form — a DIFFERENT rule from the block above, and the one whose capture was tightened from `\w+` to `[A-Z]\w*`. Present so that tightening is graded rather than assumed.

expected_entities.name: http:GET:/invoices
expected_entities.note: Produced by the Ruby EXTRACTOR, not by sinatra.yaml, and therefore unaffected by #6917 in either direction. These four rows are the fixture's held-constant axis: they were green before the fix and must stay green after it, which is what distinguishes 'the YAML rules came back' from 'something moved in Ruby extraction'.

forbidden_entities.name: do
forbidden_entities.note: #6917 forbidden arm. The `helpers <Module>` include rule used to capture `(\w+)`, which matched the `do` of `helpers do` and minted a Service entity literally named "do" next to the real block entity. It could not fire while the anchor defect kept both patterns dead; restoring `(?m)` made it reachable, so the capture was narrowed to a Ruby constant `([A-Z]\w*(?:::\w+)*)`. Reverting that narrowing puts this row back and turns the fixture red.

forbidden_entities.name: Whatever
forbidden_entities.note: #6917 forbidden arm, over-firing direction. `(?m)` is what lets `^\s*` reach an INDENTED line for the first time, so a receiver-prefixed call is now the live risk. src/receiver_calls.rb calls `server.helpers Whatever` — a valid Ruby constant that the CAPTURE would happily accept, so ONLY the line anchor keeps it out. Dropping the `^` from the helpers rule puts this entity in the graph; this row is what grades the anchor rather than the capture.

forbidden_entities.name: /never-registered
forbidden_entities.note: Appears in src/receiver_calls.rb only inside a `#` comment (`# get '/never-registered' do`). A comment opens the line with `#`, so `^\s*get` cannot reach it — this row grades that.

expected_relationships.note: #6917 recall arm for the RELATIONSHIP rules, which carry the same defect as the source patterns. The route->helper edge comes from a `(?m)^\s*(get|post|...)` pattern and produced nothing before the fix.
Held constant: an un-anchored construct, green before and after.

#6917 FINDING, and the one part of the issue's driven evidence this fixture CANNOT grade. `use Rack::Session::Cookie` lives in src/config.ru, and the indexer skips that file entirely (`processed=3 extracted=3 skipped=2` — config.ru and Gemfile are not recognised as Ruby by extension). So the `use` relationship rule is fixed and unobserved: the engine-level test TestIssue6917_UseDirectiveAfterRequire drives it directly instead. Making config.ru extractable is a separate change.
